Hi James / Elaine —

Thanks for the clear ask; we've prepared a scoped, redacted operational snapshot for Crestline. Deliverables are staged and available via SFTP and a read-only S3 manifest. Summary below (attached files are stubs in the bundle):

- hsm_attestation_2025-08-12.pdf — vendor-signed attestation (no private keys included)
- rotation_log_sample_2026Q3.csv — sample of rotation events (create/rotate/decommission), hashed operator IDs, UTC timestamps; covers Jul-Sep 2026
- operator_access_matrix.csv — roles and current holders authorized to perform key ceremonies (last reviewed 2026-09-30)
- tls_cipher_inventory_20261019.xlsx — accepted TLS versions and cipher suites for redwood-managed endpoints; shows TLS 1.2+ with preferred ciphers and TLS 1.3 enabled
- kms_config_snapshot_20261019.jsonl — config snapshot with key policies and declared wrapping algs (no secrets)

How to access: 
- SFTP (preferred): sftp://evidence.redwood.com/crestline/20261019/ — please let us know the email address to issue an OTP link; the OTP is single-use and expires in 48 hours.
- Read-only S3 manifest: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-sec-evidence/crestline/20261019/ (objects are time-limited signed URLs).

A few operational notes: 
- Our rotation cadence for primary tenant master keys is quarterly by default; tenant envelope keys rotate on customer-initiated or policy-triggered events. Emergency rotation is executed via a documented playbook and requires two operator approvals (operator + manager) and an HSM-signed wrap/unwrap audit entry.
- Key wrapping uses AES-KW (RFC 3394) for envelope keys and RSA-OAEP for partner-wrapped keys where applicable.
- In-transit protections: TLS 1.2 minimum; we have disabled weak ciphers and require forward secrecy; TLS 1.3 preferred for internal inter-node and public endpoints.

If you'd like, Marissa can host a 30-minute walkthrough with your team to go over the artifacts and answer auditor questions. Please confirm the email to send the OTP to and if we should include mapping of hashed operator IDs to full names (requires signed release).

Best,
Jonas Weber
